allocation_derivation.rule: allocation = 35 x (largest per-pair worst-case reservation at batch price, registered output cap), rounded up to the next 5 USD
allocation_derivation.worst_case_formula: (serialized request bytes + 4096) x the dearest input rate used + output cap x output rate; one token per byte is a bound, not an estimate (unchanged reservation logic)

decisions_recorded: Two final judges: GPT-6 Astra through the OpenAI API and Claude Fable 5.2 through the Anthropic API (Antonio, 16 November 2026).
One effort level for both judges and both tasks: max. OpenAI documents max for gpt-6-astra; Anthropic documents max for claude-fable-5-2.
Output caps at the model maxima: Astra max_output_tokens 128000, Fable max_tokens 128000. An output-cap stop is an invalid response with the single identical retry.
Final run: pair task only, the 35 student pairs. The whole-abstract task is out of this run.

Per-item batches: each item is its own single-request batch on both providers; all items are submitted at once and polled in parallel; a failed or invalid item gets its single identical retry at once, as a new single-request batch.

Pilot: 2 pairs, chosen by ascending sha256('oracle-pilot-20261116:' + item_id), the same 2 for both judges, sent through the synchronous full-price path. A valid pilot answer is that item's final answer when its model-visible parameters (model, instructions, prompt, schema, effort, output cap) equal the final ones; the transport difference is recorded. A pilot item that ended invalid after its registered attempts is not sent again (no third attempt).

Cutoff 11:00 CET on 16 November 2026: open batches are cancelled, completed items kept; items without a result are sent at full price through the synchronous path (OpenAI Responses streamed; Anthropic Messages streamed via _fable_once). For an item never processed that send is its first attempt; for an item that errored or was invalid it is its single identical retry.

Synchronous admission: all admissible items at once, bounded only by the per-request worst-case reservations and an adaptive cap that halves on HTTP 429 or a 5xx burst and recovers gradually (constants of adaptive_transport).
Allocations raised to the worst case: 35 x the batch worst-case reservation of one pair request, rounded up to the next 5 USD. Reservations are settled or released as soon as each item ends.

Pair binding: site instrument 61c08a1 (tag v2.1-layout-20261115) only; the 5208dfa path stays for historical items. Prompt of 39,446 characters accepted. An answer that violates a page-only rule is an invalid response, with the single identical retry, then missing. The oracle uses the final instrument only; students' cross-version answers are handled by the analysis split rule.

Rejections before generation (HTTP 429, 529/overloaded, 5xx without generation, a provider-side batch validation failure, connection errors before any output) are retried with backoff (15 s doubling, at most 300 s) until accepted and never count as an attempt. Invalid or truncated outputs keep the single identical retry. After 11:00 anything not yet accepted follows the cutoff rule.
